finding: The roles_stale term was omitted in rounds 5 and 6 on grounds each round found false, and this revision replaces those grounds with a third one that is false on the half the new mechanism provably cannot reach. §2.4 now closes with "The corpus-staleness axis is handled where it belongs, in the streak itself: §2.1's fourth no-rows cause ends the walk at a round recorded under a different corpus, so a streak never spans a corpus change and needs no condition of its own", and Non-Goal 14 restates it as "§2.1's fourth no-rows cause already ends a streak at a corpus change, so a condition over the same fact would gate twice on it". It is not the same fact. Cause 4 compares each round's stored `roles_hash` against the LATEST RECORDED ROUND's, so it only ever detects a corpus edited BETWEEN two recorded rounds. A corpus edited AFTER the latest recorded round leaves every round — the latest included — carrying the same stored hash, so no round ends the walk and the full streak is counted under a panel that is no longer in force; that is exactly the state `engine.RolesStale` detects (internal/engine/reviewstate.go:277-286 compares the latest stored hash against the current corpus hash, verified: it returns true precisely here). The two axes are disjoint, so cause 4 cannot 'gate twice' on anything RolesStale covers, and §2.1's own justification for cause 4 — "A streak counts rounds under the panel now in force" — is false in that state. On `tp audit --status` `divergence` can therefore report `spec-coverage clean 9 rounds` beside `roles_stale: true`, over rounds in which a role now in the corpus was never run, with no rule anywhere acknowledging the gap.

finding: §3.3 orders `mechanized_classes` "ascending by the same byte order §2.2 fixes for role ids" and justifies it with "a `class` is caller-supplied text under §3.1, so a mixed-case class is as reachable here as a mixed-case role id is there"; test 36 then requires the ordering to be asserted "over a fixture including one class whose leading character is uppercase". The implementer is left guessing which of the two rules to break.
